activities.title: Writing
activities.content:
Fine Motor Development
• Say: £ be ¥ buloolu niŋ ¥ balaa fasoolu mammandi la le. Ñiŋ be ǹ deemaa la le, 
ka saferoo ke kuuke. £ bulu fasoolu la bambaŋo ka mee ñaameŋ ǹ na saferoo ka 
beteyaa wo le ñaama.
• Exercise is marching: standing in place the opposite arm swings forward to the 
raised knee (left arm and right knee together). As pupils march on the spot, give 
orders: low march knees raised slightly), normal march (knees raised to half 
raised), high march (knees raised as high as possible), left turn, right turn, face 
forward.
• Alternative exercise is the crab walk: (make sure the ground is not dirty so pupils 
do not soil their clothes) sit on the ground with legs extended out in front, place 
hands by side with fingers pointed toward feet, lift body up into the air, start 
moving forward or backwards. Have pupils try for one minute then have them stop 
and rest for a minute.    
 Then have them try again for another minute.

activities.title: Vocabulary
activities.content:
Teach and Discuss New Words
• Words:    
suloo      banaanoo
• Say: Ali ŋà kuma kutoolu karaŋ, mennu si ¥ maakoyi ŋà  taaliŋo fahaamu baake. 
Kuma kummaa doolu le be taaliŋo kono, ǹ ñanta mennu karaŋ na. 
• Say the first vocabulary word, but do not write it on the board. Then have pupils 
say the word aloud. Repeat two more times.
• Ask pupils what they know about the word. Share the meaning of the word, using 
gestures or illustrations to support understanding. 
• If needed, help pupils understand the word by saying it in another language.
• Repeat all steps with remaining word.

RIGHT to LEFT and turn pages FRONT to BACK.

activities.title: Oral Language Development: Community Circle Time
activities.content:
Greeting
• Welcome pupils and have them sit in a circle. 
• Follow the normal greeting routine.
• Have the pupil that was just greeted, turn to the pupil on their right and greet 
them. This continues all the way around the circle.
Theme Discussion
• Before school starts, bring in two items related to the theme to show the pupils. 
Put the items in the center of the circle. If no items are available, draw two 
pictures on the board instead.
• Say: Ñiŋ lookuŋo, ǹ na karaŋ kuŋo mu '' Naakoo'' le ti. Feŋolu mennu be jaŋ ì be ¥ 
na karaŋ kuŋo le la. 
• Hold up one of the items from the center of the circle.
• Say: Munne  mu ñiŋ ti?
• Call on a pupil at random to answer. 
• Say: I si munne  fo noo n ye ñiŋ to.?
• Call on 2-3 pupils at random to answer. Repeat with the second item. 
• Say: Mamaa ko a ye ko, laa waatoo siita le
• Give pupils one minute to think, even close their eyes to picture their response. 
Then choose one of the following options for discussion: call on pupils at random, 
Turn and Talk (have pupils turn to a pupil next to them), go around the circle and 
allow every pupil to answer (only if the answer is short), or have pupils take turns 
acting out answers.
• Encourage pupils to bring in their own items relating to the theme throughout the 
week.
